title: AI auto-router must fall back on model-level error
desc: Agent.cmd and the wk auto-router (--model auto) must FALL BACK to the next candidate model when the chosen model returns a MODEL-LEVEL error (rate_limit, overloaded, model-unavailable, API failure) -- never fail the whole delegation. Final fallback is a cheap always-available model (haiku, zero Claude quota). A delegation should always land on SOME model.
steps: PROBLEM: --model auto selected a model, that model returned a MODEL-LEVEL error (rate_limit_error / overloaded / model-unavailable / transient API failure), and the dispatch FAILED instead of trying the next candidate -- the delegation was lost and the orchestrator had to retry manually.

FIX: on a model-level error, the auto-router retries the SAME task with the next candidate in the routing chain, and the FINAL fallback is the cheapest always-available model (haiku) -- so a delegation always lands on some model rather than dying.

SCOPE: fall back ONLY on model/infra errors (rate-limit, overloaded, unavailable, network). Do NOT fall back on a TASK error -- a task that ran and failed is a real result to surface, not a routing failure. Distinguish model-error from task-error before retrying.

CHAIN: route by capability first (cheap for survey, mid for synthesis, strong for judgment), then degrade on error down to haiku. Respect per-tier budgets (codex weekly, Claude weekly) when picking the next candidate.
WHERE: the Agent.cmd / wk auto-router wrapper plus the harness autoroute logic (wkharness-common). Log each fallback hop so the orchestrator can see which model actually answered.
author: claude
